With a little more room to think than yesterday, I looked again. The whole castle seemed to be holding itself stiff.

The skin of the soldiers going back and forth was all bristled, and their eyeballs were red from overstretched nerves. The civil officials and ladies-in-waiting were busy with work, but now and then they looked at nothing, shivering a little, as if a cold draft was blowing only for them.

It was too early to let the assassination of Lord General Moriuji fade into the past. Assassination, that is, about eighty percent likely. Its cold rain was plainly falling on all their minds.

This was bad for their health. It was not good for me either.

With vigilance higher than usual, the task given to Ichijou and me became one step harder. Not that carelessness had been in the plan. Still, 'I did not mean to be careless' would be a poor defense afterward. I had to keep a stricter watch. From any side, at any moment, our identity could leak out.

みれば、城内の空気はいかにも硬い。

　行き交う兵士らの皮膚は毛羽立ち、眼球は神経の昂
りを示して充血している。
　文官、女官達は業務に没頭しつつも、どこか薄寒そ
うな様子で時折あらぬ方を見やる。

　過去の事件として記憶を風化させてしまうにはまだ
早過ぎる、大将領護氏暗殺――であろう、八割方――

られた任務を一段と困難にする。
　元々そんなつもりはないにしろ、油断を厳に戒める
必要があった。いつ何から正体が露顕するか知れない。

So the boy carrying a ruler's destiny was now being <ruby>attended<rt>attended</rt></ruby> by noble ladies, protected by mighty warriors, and playing with a <ruby>ball<rt>ball</rt></ruby>.

It was about the size of a human head, with a black-and-white pattern.

...<ruby>Football<rt>Soccer</rt></ruby>, then. Nowhere near the level of its native Europe, but even in Yamato it was gaining popularity. The special feature of the game is that hands are mostly forbidden, and the ball is handled with the feet.

Eleven on one side, eleven on the other, competing for points: that was the proper arrangement. Here, twenty-one players were not in the picture at all. Shirou Kuniuji was kicking the ball up by himself.

It was probably the basic practice called juggling: you keep kicking, and the ball must not touch the ground. As for Shirou Ashikaga's juggling... achchha, let me be polite. It was not good.

In Tokai, where football was most popular in Yamato, two hundred, three hundred touches were nothing unusual for a schoolboy who played. This boy mostly lost his balance and dropped the ball after a few touches, ten or so on a good day. He seemed not to know the knack at all.

His reflexes did not look poor. Someone only had to tell him how. But from these ladies, what instruction was going to come? Kick the ball: "well played." Drop the ball: "magnificent." Same marks for both answers; how was the boy to find the wrong one?

The guard warriors did not even bother with flattery. Probably they were concentrating on duty, but there was also a cold distance in them. Something like a nuisance.

Their faces were behind their helmets, but I could guess the message. If only he would stay indoors, the guarding would be so much easier.

王者の宿命を背負う彼は今、高貴な女達に<ruby>傅<rt>かしず</rt></ruby>かれ、
強剛の武者に守護されながら――<ruby>球<rt>ボール</rt></ruby>で遊んでいる。
　およそ人頭大の、白黒模様の球だった。

　……<ruby>蹴球<rt>サッカー</rt></ruby>か。
　本場欧州とは比べものにならないにせよ、大和でも
人気を獲得しつつある球技である。腕の使用を原則と
して禁じ、足で球を扱う点に特徴がある。

　本来は十一人のチーム二つで得点を争う競技だが、
勿論いま目の前でそれが繰り広げられているという事
はない。
　四郎邦氏は一人で球を蹴り上げて遊んでいる。

　リフティングと呼ばれる基礎練習だろう。
　球を地面に落とさぬよう蹴り続けるものだ……が、
足利四郎のそれは世辞にも上手くなかった。

　大和で最も蹴球が盛んな東海地方の競技少年であれ
ば二百三百とこなすのも珍しくないところ、彼は大抵
数回、良くても十回余りで均衡を失い落としている。
　どうもコツをまるで知らないようだ。

　運動神経は悪くなさそうである。誰かが適切なアド
バイスをすれば伸びるだろう。
　しかし球を蹴ろうが落とそうがお上手です、お見事
ですとしか言わない女達にそれは期待できまい。

　警備の武者らは阿諛すら口にせずにいる。
　任務に集中しているのであろうが――どこか冷たい
よそよそしさもあった。どこか迷惑げな。

　兜に覆われた素顔が覗けるわけではないが、何とは
なし察しはついた。
　屋内に篭もってくれていれば警護も楽なものを――
と言いたいのであろう。

The boy was not so dull that he could feel pleased with the ladies' praise, thin as cheap face powder, and not so thick that he missed the cold air of the guards. That expression of his understood both.

Still he went on, probably because even this small time of play was precious to him. Was he ordinarily shut away behind heavy walls and roofs, just as the guards wanted?

It fitted his station, his rank and the present situation. For a growing boy, it was a cruel treatment all the same.

Seeing that little court noble keep up his lonely game with a hard face was painful.

An itch・・・-like feeling came on the top of my head.

Without looking, I knew that one dragoon had moved above me. I also knew that a 7.7 mmmillimeter machine gun was now pointed at me.

At the first slightly dangerous movement, my whole body would be made into a beehive.

No, not even the shape of a beehive would remain. Only a lump of fleshmincemeat.

Holding the ball in her arms, the princess looked at Kuniuji. Her face was complicated beyond easy words.

Rokuhara was her mortal enemy. Just because she tried not to show it, resentment would not vanish.

Shirou Kuniuji Ashikaga stood at the top of that enemy. If the shogunate had any guilt, he could even be called the holder of all of that guilt, although he was not yet in that seat at the time of the Okabe rebellion.

Even if Princess Sakurako searched to the very end of the three thousand great thousand worlds, she would not find any reason to feel anything but hostility for him.

Yet, she must have understood also.

That the one standing in front of her was only a boy who had been playing without thinking anything. By strange chance, it was I who had made him so.

Even if she fixed a hidden blade in her gaze, no blade would strike back. It would only pass through him without resistance... through the heart also.

Could the orphan princess of Okabe do that?

The princess held out the ball. Hesitantly, Kuniuji put out his hand and took it.

A princess of a fallen house.

A boy who would be the ruler.

For that one instant, their fingertips seemed to touch lightly.

Princess Sakurako bowed and went back. Inside the movement of turning away, she slipped in, so lightly, a greeting for me—◆and at her rueful smile, which seemed to ask "What are you doing?", I could only give the same rueful smile.

Really. What exactly was I doing?

en.html:
The boy trembled, his face struck by shock. The daughter of the family destroyed by his Rokuhara, by his shogunate's army.

She was leaving with her back half turned to us. She looked composed. Not perfectly, though. The stiffness showing at the edges of her movements seemed the shape of her heart itself.

The daughter of Yoritsuna Okabe was being led before the senior ministers of the shogunate. A pleasant meeting could not be waiting for her.

Most likely they would inquire into what Ms Iwata had told me, the existence of anti-shogunate elements planning to seize Sakurako.

They would hardly put her to torture, but questioning beyond all reason was quite possible.

In Fudaraku she had no ally.

The princess walking away was beautiful. It was the beauty of one lonely flower blooming alone on a wasteland.

衝撃を受けた面持ちで、少年が体を震わせた。
　――彼の六波羅、彼の幕軍が滅ぼし去った一族の、
娘。

　彼女はこちらに斜め後姿を見せる格好で離れゆく。
　沈着な様子ではあった。完璧ではなかったけれども。
身ごなしの端々に覗く強張りは、姫の内心そのものに
思えた。

　岡部頼綱の娘が、幕閣の面々の前へ連行されてゆく
のだ。
　心楽しい会合が待つ筈もなかった。

　おそらくは、岩田女史が俺に伝えた事――桜子奪取
を謀る反幕勢力の存在について、査問を行うのだろう。
　まさか拷問には掛けられまいが、度を超した尋問に
なる事は充分に有り得る。

　この普陀楽に、彼女の味方はいないのだから。
　
　去りゆく姫は美しかった。
　荒野にただ一輪で咲く、孤独な花の美しさがあった。
